in_arabic.name: قائم
in_arabic.meaning: قائم کا مطلب ہے وہ جو قائم رہتا ہے، مستحکم رہتا ہے
in_arabic.long_meaning: قائم (Qaaim) کا نام اس صفت سے ماخوذ ہے جو اللہ تعالیٰ کی صفات میں سے ایک ہے، یعنی وہ جو ہمیشہ قائم اور مستحکم ہے۔ یہ نام قائم رہنے، پائیدار ہونے اور استحکام کی خصوصیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ قرآن کریم میں بھی اس صفت کا ذکر کیا گیا ہے، جیسے کہ 'وہی ہے جو قائم ہے، کوئی تبدیلی نہیں ہونے دیتا' (سورہ الحدید، آیت 3)۔ اس نام کا انتخاب کرنے کا مطلب ہے کہ والدین اپنے بچے کے لیے اللہ کی اس صفت کو خواہاں ہیں۔

in_urdu.name: قائم
in_urdu.meaning: قائم کا مطلب ہے وہ جو قائم رہتا ہے، پائیدار رہتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: قائم (Qaaim) کا نام عربی زبان کی 'ق-و-م' (Q-W-M) جڑ سے بنا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کھڑا ہونا، قائم ہونا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں بھی اہمیت رکھتا ہے، کیونکہ 'قائم' اللہ تعالیٰ کے ناموں میں سے ایک ہے۔ اس نام کا روحانی مطلب ہے کسی چیز کی پائیداری اور استحکام کی دعا کرنا۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لیے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں، یہ نام روایتی اور مذہبی اہمیت کا حامل ہے۔

in_hindi.name: क़ायम
in_hindi.meaning: क़ायम का अर्थ है जो स्थापित रहता है, स्थिर रहता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: क़ायम (Qaaim) नाम की उत्पत्ति 'क़-व-म' (Q-W-M) अरबी मूल से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है सीधा खड़ा होना या स्थापित होना। इस नाम का चयन करना माता-पिता की यह इच्छा होती है कि उनका बच्चा हमेशा स्थिर और मजबूत बने। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम धार्मिक और पारंपरिक महत्व रखता है, और अक्सर बच्चों को आध्यात्मिक अर्थों में दिया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: قائم
in_pashto.meaning: قائم معنی یې دا دی چې هغه څوک چې ولاړ وي، پايښ وي
in_pashto.long_meaning: قائم (Qaaim) نوم د عربي 'ق-و-م' (Q-W-M) ريښې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې معنی يې ولاړ يا پايښ کيدل دي. په پښتنو او افغانانو کې، دا نوم د الهي صفاتو څخه يو له مهمو نومونو څخه ګڼل کيږي. دا نوم د پايښتوب او استقامت دعا کوي. په پښتو کلتور کې، دا نوم په ديني او ټولنيزو مراسمو کې کارول کيږي.

in_english.name: Qaaim
in_english.meaning: Qaaim means the one who stands firm, eternal, and stable
in_english.long_meaning: The name Qaaim (Qā'im) originates from the Arabic root 'Q-W-M', which means to stand, to rise, or to be steadfast. In Islamic theology, Qaaim is one of the attributes of Allah, signifying His eternal and unchanging nature. The Quran references this attribute in several verses, emphasizing the permanence and stability of God's existence. As a given name, Qaaim symbolizes the wish for the bearer to embody these qualities of resilience, permanence, and spiritual steadfastness. Across various Muslim cultures, the name holds significant religious and spiritual connotations.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic context, the name "Qaaim" signifies an individual who takes the mantle of leadership and responsibility seriously. Historically, Qaamis were the rulers or leaders who provided direction and protection to their communities. Today, the name can be given to children, acknowledging their potential to lead and make a positive impact on those around them.

It is a call to action, an invitation to govern oneself with wisdom, integrity, and self-control, ultimately leading to a closer connection to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Al-Qa'im bi-amrihil-lah (The one established upon Allah's command) was a title given to the twelfth Imam in Shia Islam. He is believed to be in occultation and will reappear at the end of time to fill the world with justice.
historical_references.context: The period of the Twelfth Imam in Shia Islam, also known as the Major Occultation, began around the 10th century CE and continues to the present day.

historical_references.reference: The first Khalifah bearing the title 'Qa'im' was Caliph Al-Qa'im bi-amrihil-lah (r. 833-842 CE). He was the eleventh Abbasid Caliph and focused on reaffirming the authority of the caliphate following the Anarchy of the Abbasids.
historical_references.context: The period of the Abbasid Caliphate, following the Umayyad Dynasty, marked a major turning point in Islamic history. The title 'Qa'im' was used to emphasize the caliph's role as the 'upholder' or 'establisher' of the Islamic state.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Qaaim' in modern context refers to a legitimate ruler or political leader in the Islamic tradition. This title holds significant importance in Islamic political discourse as well as in various aspects of Islamic scholarship and art and culture. The term 'Qaaim' is derived from the Arabic root 'q-m-m', which means 'to remain' or 'to stay'. In the Islamic context, it signifies the one who maintains the balance, justice, and peace in the Muslim community. The title is often used interchangeably with the terms 'Caliph' or 'Imam'. Historically, the Islamic State was ruled by a Qaaim or Caliph, who was considered the political and spiritual leader of the Muslim community. However, in contemporary times, the concept of a Qaaim has evolved beyond the political realm and is also used in Islamic scholarship and art and culture to describe individuals who uphold and maintain the Islamic traditions and values.
